text:
A: Hiya, hello! Can you hear me alright?
B: Yeah, fine. Darren.
A: Daniel, nice to meet you. I'm in Newark, East Midlands. I'm a director at a lettings firm, family business, so I sort of run the day-to-day. Where are you, sorry?
B: Halesowen. West Midlands. I work at a garden centre, part time.
A: Oh, nice. Is that good, a garden centre? I always think it'd be quite relaxing.
B: It's alright. Older regulars, mostly. They want to know about compost and they want a chat. And they've started on the Christmas grotto already, so I'm selling pansies next to a plastic reindeer.
A: Ha! In September?
B: September. Every year.
A: That's mad. Er, I think you spoke to Craig, the Leigh one, did you? He said I said cob.
B: He did, yeah. Cob, barm, bap. We were going through them all. It's a bap where I am.
A: My girlfriend says bap and all! We argue about it. I get a ham and cheese cob from the bakery by the office every day, and I'm not changing now.
B: No, you stick with it.
A: Do you have kids? I saw the calendar on your fridge, the school holidays.
B: Two. Kieran's fifteen, Ellie's eleven. My wife's a healthcare assistant on hospital shifts, so I do the school runs and the cooking and that, around her rota. It works, mostly. Kieran's hard work at the minute, to be fair. Doesn't want to talk to his dad about anything.
A: Yeah, I can imagine. I was probably the same with mine. I still live at home, actually, with my mum and dad, which is, er, a bit embarrassing at thirty. Saving for a deposit, though.
B: Nothing embarrassing in that. Prices how they are.
A: That's what I tell myself. I'm on Rightmove every night, honestly, just looking at houses in the villages I can't afford.
B: I do that with Google Maps. Plan trips. Norway, round Scotland. Never go.
A: Ha, same thing really, isn't it. What do you cook, then, if you do the cooking?
B: Curries, mostly. From scratch. Got a cupboard full of spice jars. And a big Sunday dinner.
A: Oh, I love a curry. Chicken bhuna every Friday, same takeaway. I'm not adventurous, mind. I'd never make one myself. Sunday dinner's my mum's, and her roast potatoes are, honestly, unbeatable.
B: What does she do, goose fat?
A: Do you know, I don't actually know. I've never asked. I should, really.
B: You should. I wish I'd asked my dad more stuff, before he went. Not roasties, like. His work. He was in the chain works in Cradley Heath, and I've read all these books about it since, and he could've just told me.
A: Oh, I'm sorry. That's, yeah. My nan's not been well, actually, and I keep thinking that. Boxing Day's always at hers.
B: Ask her things, then, while you can. That's all I'd say.
A: Yeah. No, definitely. I will. Are you a football man, or
B: Wolves.
A: Ah, Forest for me. We'll not talk about the last time we played, then.
